world.name: The Litany Sea
world.tagline: A war over the nature of truth, fought with salt and brine on the corpse of a god, with a clock everyone can hear.
world.premise: When the leviathan-deity Veyl was slain in the deep past, it did not bleed — it wept, and its grief filled the basin of the world to become the Litany Sea, an ocean of brine in which every drop held a remembered moment. Now the Sea is dying: the rust-red sun has not set in living memory, and the brine is evaporating, receding thigh-deep then ankle-deep then gone, crystallizing as it goes into salt-glass that fossilizes real history — each crystal a moment you can re-live, sell, edit, set forever, or shatter so that it never happened at all. Across this drying flat wade the memory-archivists, rival orders who have realized that whichever version of the past is still crystallized when the…
world.twist: The leviathan-deity Veyl is not dead — it is grieving, and the Litany Sea is not its corpse but its open, weeping wound, still dreaming. Every crystal is a tear it has not finished crying, and the "history" the archivists fight to fix or erase is in fact Veyl actively re-remembering its own life as it dies, which is why the salt-dead keep rising: they are the god flinching at moments it cannot let go. The brine is not evaporating from heat — it is being wept out, and when the last pool dries,…

mechanics.name: The Long Toll (the living, audible clock)
mechanics.concept: The receding brine is a shared doomsday clock every faction reads identically. The Sea is genuinely alive during play: each round the tide marker advances one step on a fixed track audible as the 'Toll,' and the entire board physically transforms — Brine-deep zones recede to Dry, exposing crystals;…

mechanics.name: Custody & Collateral (capture WITHOUT breaking)
mechanics.concept: Crystals are fragile, irreplaceable, lore-bearing OBJECTS, not abstract tokens. The core tension is seizing or protecting a specific thing without shattering it in the crossfire — collateral damage as the central dilemma. You cannot win by destroying the board; you win by having intact, controlled…

mechanics.name: The Dreaming Grief (re-dreaming & board corruption)
mechanics.concept: Veyl's grief still dreams, and the salt-dead — Reliquiae, ghosts who exist only while their crystal stays solid — are the crisis given a face. The more the board dries and the more crystals shatter, the more the god flinches and re-remembers its dead, so the horde scales with the very corruption…

terms.meaning: The shared, audible countdown of the receding brine — measured in 'tides' (game rounds). Every faction reads the same Toll; when it strikes dry, the table's…
A crystallized memory. A single fossilized moment of real history, fragile and irreplaceable. A named, lore-bearing objective crystal is called a Litany;…
The two states of any board zone. Brine-deep zones are flooded and movement-slowing but protect crystals from shattering; Dry zones are fast and lethal —…
The act of making a crystal permanent — 'setting' a memory so it can never be edited, sold, or shattered for the rest of the game. The Mnemarchs' sacred verb…
When the receding tide tries to erase a Reliquia, the god's grief sometimes re-remembers it, returning the model to play. The Sediment's resource and the…
The end-state epistemological scoring: which faction's ontology of the past — fixed, erased, sold, or freed — controls the most crystallized history when the…
In-world slang for an archivist who has re-lived too many crystals and can no longer tell their own memories from the Sea's. The smell of iodine on the flat…

factions.name: The Mnemarchs (Order of the Set Hour)
factions.identity: Slow, immovable, anvil-and-ritual control. Nearly every unit Cannot Run and is Salt-Stiffened, so the Mnemarchs cannot chase — they pick a wet zone, plant a bastion (Verdigris Wardens carrying Cushion of the Brine), bring Witnesses and the Sealing Choir, and try to complete the Set ritual before the Toll dries the ground out from under them. The core tension is timing: Set too early and you waste sacraments on uncontested crystals; wait for safety and the tide may strip the wet zone first. Tempo-poor but produces the only truly unkillable scoring on the table.
factions.playstyle: The Set Hour — the ONLY way in the game to make a crystal permanent. A binary, irreversible seal that can be performed only on a crystal in a Brine-deep (wet) zone, with two Witnesses. Once Set, the crystal can never be touched by anyone (including the Mnemarchs) and counts for…
factions.colorMotif: Bone-white and verdigris bronze — bleached vestments, oxidized reliquary fittings, salt-rimed gold.

signatureRule.name: The Set Hour
signatureRule.text: Once per round, a Mnemarch model in base contact with a Held Litany or salt-glass crystal that is in a Brine-deep zone may perform the Set Hour instead of acting: declare it and place a Set marker on the crystal. A Set crystal can NEVER again be Held, edited, sold, shattered,…

lore.origin: The Mnemarchs began with a single wading hermit at the First Recession — the one who first re-lived a crystal and learned the past could be touched. But where others felt the thrill of a thing that could be changed, this hermit, an old reliquary-keeper named Osseil the Stilled, felt only horror: if the past can be edited, then nothing is true, and a world with no fixed truth is a world already dead. Osseil knelt in the shrinking margin and did the opposite of editing — they…
lore.culture: Mnemarch culture is liturgical, slow, and obsessively rigorous. They wear salt-stiffened vestments that crust harder with every crystal they Set, so that a senior archivist can barely move — rigidity is rank, and a fully-Set elder is a walking reliquary who has not bent at the waist in years. They speak in 'attestations': nothing is true until two witnesses have re-lived a crystal and sworn it matches, word for word, breath for breath. To them, editing is heresy and selling…
lore.whyTheyFight: The Mnemarchs fight because the Verdict is coming and they alone believe the past has intrinsic worth that must not be touched. If the Brine-Factors win, the god's last memory will be a forgery edited to suit a buyer. If the Ash Iconoclasts win, there will be no last memory at all — the god dies mid-sentence, erased. If the Sediment wins, every fixed truth dissolves and nothing was ever real. The Mnemarchs cannot abide any of these. They fight to Set the true moments before…
lore.leadership: The Order is led by the Set Hierarch, currently Antiphon Vael, called the Unbending — an elder so thoroughly Set in salt-vestment that they are carried into battle on a reliquary palanquin, unable to walk, and speak only in confirmed attestations. Beneath the Hierarch are the Two Witnesses, paired officers who must both agree before any crystal is Set; a Mnemarch force that loses one Witness fights on, but can no longer Set anything until a new pairing is sworn — a…
lore.homeland: The Mnemarchs have no true homeland, because they refuse to claim ground — ground is not history. Their seat is the Set Hour itself, a vast Litany-cathedral built entirely from crystals they have Set, hauled inward from the receding margins over generations and stacked into vaulted naves of salt-glass that ring like bells when the wind crosses them. It is mobile in the way a glacier is mobile, dragged tide by tide toward the last pools as the Sea retreats, so that the…

units.name: Attesting Acolytes
units.flavor: Junior archivists who wade out, lay hands on a crystal, and die in attesting silence rather than let go.

units.name: Chime-Wardens
units.flavor: Still-standing marksmen who fire only sworn, attested shots and make the approach to a guarded pool cost bodies.

units.name: Verdigris Wardens
units.flavor: Bronze-crusted veterans so oxidized they ring green when struck; you do not push them off the objective, you wait for the water to leave.

units.name: The Sealing Choir
units.flavor: Robed singers who perform the Set Hour as liturgy, racing the drying Toll and gambling on a single die that the moment Sets rather than shatters.

units.name: Pilgrim-Bearers of the Sealed Vault
units.flavor: Stooped bearers hauling one fixed truth out of the crossfire, defenseless and utterly devoted, each a walking reliquary.

units.name: Lector of the Permitted Truth
units.flavor: A witness-priest who recites the day's allowable truths and re-lives crystals to attest them, steadily going iodine-blind on the Sea's edge.

units.name: Reliquary Sentinels
units.role: Static heavy fire-anchor / point-defense gun crew
units.flavor: An immobile gun-shrine bolted into the pool floor that punishes the deep-water approach with a single heavy, attested shot.

characters.name: Antiphon Vael, the Unbending (Set Hierarch)
characters.title: Set Hierarch on Reliquary Palanquin / Warlord
characters.flavor: An elder so Set into salt-vestment they can no longer walk, carried on a palanquin of crystals they sealed decades ago, slow as a glacier and the last thing standing in the dry.

characters.name: The Two Witnesses (Concord & Antiphony)
characters.title: Paired named support characters / win-condition enablers
characters.flavor: Paired officers who must both live and both agree for any truth to be Set, finishing one another's attestations; kill one and the Order's sacrament freezes.

factions.name: The Ash Iconoclasts (the Shattering)
factions.identity: Hyper-aggressive, fragile, board-burning glass cannons. Cheap expendable bodies (Slag-Pick Penitents at 8 pts), We Keep No Relics and Faith Without Memory mean they never hold or score crystals the normal way — they advance the Scour and force impossible choices: the enemy guarding an Exposed prize must either stand in front of the Breaking Volley (and die) or step away (and let the crystal shatter). They cannot work wet zones (water auto-passes), so they live and die on punishing whatever the Toll dries out. Tempo-rich, durability-poor.
factions.playstyle: Collateral Is the Point / Breaking Volley — uniquely, they aim AT the crystal on purpose. On a declared Breaking Volley against an enemy in/adjacent to an Exposed crystal, EVERY die (hits and misses) is also rolled against the crystal, and a natural 5 or 6 Shatters it (everyone…
factions.colorMotif: Charcoal and ember-orange — scorched grey robes, burnt-iodine smoke, glowing crack-lines like cooling slag.

signatureRule.name: Collateral Is the Point
signatureRule.text: When any Ash Iconoclast unit shoots at an enemy model that is in or adjacent to an Exposed crystal's zone, BEFORE rolling the attack the controlling player may declare the shot a Breaking Volley. A Breaking Volley resolves normally against the enemy target — but EVERY die in the…

lore.origin: The first Iconoclast was the wading hermit of the First Recession — the same one who, in every other order's telling, founded the practice of re-living crystals. The Mnemarchs canonize that hermit as a saint of memory. The Iconoclasts know the rest of the story: after touching a thousand fossilized moments, the hermit went iodine-blind, could no longer tell their own grief from the Sea's, and understood the unbearable truth before anyone else — the crystals are not relics,…
lore.culture: A culture of deliberate forgetting, which makes it a culture with almost no internal memory — and they consider that a sacrament, not a flaw. Iconoclasts do not keep records, do not name their dead, and burn (in iodine-fire, the only fire that takes on the wet flat) anything that threatens to become a relic. They speak in the present tense exclusively; to use the past tense is a minor heresy, a small act of letting a moment harden. New initiates are made to shatter a crystal…
lore.whyTheyFight: They fight to lose — and they have made peace with that, which is what makes them terrifying. The Iconoclasts cannot author the god's last memory and do not want to; an Iconoclast who 'won the Verdict' would have failed utterly, because winning means a version of the past survived, and survival is the disease. Their entire war effort is negation: to ensure that when the last pool dries, NO ontology is intact, that the god finishes its dying thought on a blank, that Veyl…
lore.leadership: The order is led by the Choir of Last Voices, a council of the most profoundly iodine-blind among them — archivists who have re-lived so many crystals that they have no remaining sense of which memories are their own, and who therefore (the Iconoclasts believe) hear the god's grief most clearly, undiluted by self. The Choir does not give orders so much as point at what must be silenced; they are carried into battle on salt-litters because most can no longer reliably tell…
lore.homeland: The Iconoclasts have no homeland and forbid themselves one, because a home is a place that remembers you. They live in the Scour — not a location but a moving condition, the band of freshly-Dried flat directly behind the receding tide, where the brine has just left and the salt-glass is youngest and most brittle and the salt-dead rise thickest. They follow the recession like carrion-walkers follow an army, always in the wettest-newest edge of the Dry, breaking the…

units.name: Slag-Pick Penitent
units.role: Cheap aggressive line infantry / glass-cannon body
units.flavor: Fresh from the joining rite, scarred and swinging a glowing pick; they die cheap and do not remember the man who just fell beside them.

units.name: Scour-Walker
units.flavor: Bare-footed zealots who reach the youngest, most brittle salt-glass first, breaking what the receding water just left behind.

units.name: Iodine Censer-Thrower
units.flavor: Lobs censers that bloom in sweet acrid fire — useless on armour, ruinous on glass; it aims at the Litany and lets the guard decide whether to keep standing in front of it.

units.name: Cantor-Breaker
units.flavor: A zealot just shy of full blindness who finds a Litany's fracture-note by ear; where the Cantor-Breaker sings, the salt-glass wants to come apart.

units.name: Voice of the Last Hour
units.flavor: A profoundly blind Choir veteran who marches toward any silence it can hear; whatever is loud — friend, foe, or prize — it breaks.

units.name: Ash-Anchorite
units.flavor: A solitary penitent who re-lives one chosen crystal until they know precisely how it must break, then arrives alone to unmake it before anyone knew they were there.

units.name: Glass-Wraith Detonator
units.flavor: A penitent who has made a bomb of their own body, closing to a prize and simply ending — taking themselves, the crystal, and whatever guarded it out of history in one bloom of sweet fire.

units.name: Litter of the Choir
units.flavor: A blind Voice of the Choir borne on a salt-litter by chained Penitents; it cannot see the battle and does not need to — it hears the god's grief and points at what must go quiet next.

units.name: Cooling-Slag Cantor
units.flavor: A Cantor who travels with the Choir of Last Voices and has stopped pretending to fight a war; declares a zone and lets everything in it — including its own line — eat the volley.

characters.name: Vael-Who-Is-Nothing-Yet
characters.title: First Cantor of the Cooling-Slag Choir, the Quiet She Heard
characters.flavor: She has touched so many crystals she no longer knows her own grief from the Sea's; she chases the one clean silence she heard the day she shattered her first Litany, and breaks the world toward it.

characters.name: Korrun the Match
characters.title: Last-Voice Penitent, Burned Everything in the Joining and Came Up Laughing
characters.flavor: He shattered the crystal of his dearest memory at dawn and is fighting in the raw open wound of it, racing to make the whole world feel the hole he just put in himself.
characters.rule: Spend Me Like a Struck Match

factions.name: The Brine-Factors (the Salt Exchange)
factions.identity: Mobile, opportunistic, economic tempo. Fast cheap snatchers (Cutpurses, Reach-Runners, Skiff-Reach Corsairs) dart in, liquidate contested crystals, and bank Coin to bribe, edit, and reinforce reactively. The constant brutal decision is liquidity vs. presence: a sold crystal is safe and counts but is off the board doing nothing, and you can never sit still on your wealth — spend to zero and you collapse. They reward kinetic, never-moored play and out-tempo opponents by removing the prize before anyone can break or seal it.
factions.playstyle: The Open Ledger — they do not score by holding crystals, they score by SELLING them. Disengaging a Factor from a Loose/Held crystal lifts it off the board into the Hold (untouchable, scoring) and earns 1 Coin; Coin is the fuel for every other Factor rule and can be spent during…
factions.colorMotif: Brass and deep teal — patinaed brass scales, ledger-ink teal sashes, glittering coin-cut salt.

signatureRule.name: The Open Ledger
signatureRule.text: The Brine-Factors do not score crystals by holding them — they score by SELLING them. Maintain a single visible pool of Coin (use physical coin-cut salt tokens so the board, not bookkeeping, shows your wealth). EARN: any time a Factor model in base contact with a Loose or Held…

lore.origin: The Brine-Factors did not begin as archivists at all. They were the salvage-crews and bilge-runners who skimmed the receding margins for whatever the other three orders left behind — cracked salt-glass too damaged to enshrine, off-cuts the Mnemarchs deemed unsanctifiable, shards the Iconoclasts hadn't gotten around to breaking. They were scavengers of scavengers. The turn came when a wading hauler named Cassine Lir re-lived a half-spoiled crystal of a battle that had never…
lore.culture: A mercantile guild dressed as a religion of the deal, or a religion dressed as a guild — the Factors themselves no longer bother to distinguish, since the distinction doesn't price differently. Every Factor carries a ledger-stone, a slab of dark salt-glass on which their debts and credits are crystallized; to die owing more than you're owed is the only true Factor disgrace, and the dead are appraised before they are mourned. They speak in the cant of the Exchange: a friend…
lore.whyTheyFight: They fight because the Sea is the final liquidation sale of all history, and a closing sale waits for no one. The Mnemarchs want to fix the past, the Iconoclasts to erase it, the Sediment to free it — all of which, to a Factor, are different ways of taking inventory off the market and destroying its value. The Factors fight to keep the past liquid, tradeable, and theirs to price, right up until the Toll strikes dry. They do not especially want any particular version of the…
lore.leadership: The Exchange is run by the Counting House, a rotating quorum of Senior Factors whose authority is measured purely in the size of their book. Pre-eminent among them is the Iodine Comptroller, Vael Surr-of-the-Open-Ledger, who is said to have re-lived so many edited crystals that she remembers seventeen contradictory childhoods and bills the discrepancy to a holding account. She does not give orders; she quotes prices, and a Factor who refuses her price simply discovers that…
lore.homeland: The Factors have no homeland because a homeland is an immobile asset, and the Factors do not hold immobile assets. Their 'territory' is the Salt Exchange itself — a floating, ever-relocating bazaar of lashed skiffs, ledger-barges, and tide-sledges that follows the receding waterline so that it is always moored at the exact margin where fresh crystals are forming. Wherever the brine is leaving fastest, the Exchange is already there, planks down, lamps lit, prices chalked,…

units.name: Cutpurse Wavewalkers
units.flavor: Touch a crystal, liquidate it, and be three zones gone before the splash reacts — they bill you for the inconvenience.

units.name: Skiff-Reach Corsairs
units.flavor: Flank, liquidate whatever the front line was guarding, and vanish across water no one else crosses at speed.

units.name: Factor-Clerks of the Open Book
units.flavor: They never throw a punch — they Edit the salt under your feet and watch your victory revalue to a loss in their margins.

units.name: Ironbound Bodyguard-Clerks
units.flavor: A wall of ledger-armor around the wallet — debt-collectors who collect in person and never let the Coin out of arm's reach.

units.name: The Iodine-Blind
units.flavor: They can no longer tell their past from yours and have monetized the confusion, salting the flat with lies until the truth has no quotable price.

units.name: The Hauler-Sledge
units.role: Heavy support / mobile Hold / objective denial
units.flavor: A groaning sledge that scoops crystals by the armful — slow, greedy, and impossible to rob, because the merchandise is already gone.

units.name: Reach-Runner Outriders
units.flavor: All velocity, no reserves — thin-book runners who exist to touch, sell, and be gone before they cost anything to lose.

characters.name: Vael Surr, the Iodine Comptroller
characters.title: Faction Warlord / Coin Generator / Market-Controller
characters.flavor: She remembers seventeen childhoods and bills the discrepancy to a holding account — and intends to be the last solvent thing the Sea ever sees.

characters.name: The Auctioneer-Adept
characters.title: Hero Support / Tempo-Control / Bribe Specialist
characters.flavor: Wherever the Auctioneer stands the past goes to the highest bidder, and the bidding never stops until the Toll strikes dry.

factions.name: The Sediment (the Re-Dreaming)
factions.identity: Attritional swarm that feeds on the game's own decay. Dirt-cheap expendable bodies (Wadeling Drift at 6 pts, Murmur-Host at 7) are spent like water because the drying board pays them back. They smother objectives, Drown The Prize to deny Sets, and grow stronger precisely when opponents are most active — Iconoclast shatters and Mnemarch crystal-fights both refill Grief. The core skill is managing the two-tide erasure clock so the recursion engine never actually empties. Durability-rich through recursion, individually disposable.
factions.playstyle: The Re-Dreaming — they never lose a model, they send it back. Casualties go to a Re-Dreaming pile; at the start of each round (after the Toll) Grief tokens are spent 1-for-1 to AUTO-RETURN them to any Dry zone, no roll, no scatter. The Grief pool fills from the whole table's…
factions.colorMotif: Pale salt-grey and bruise-violet — translucent crystalline flesh, deep-water violet shadow, iridescent brine-sheen.

signatureRule.name: The Re-Dreaming
signatureRule.text: The Sediment never loses a Reliquia — it only sends one back to be re-remembered. When any Reliquia model is removed as a casualty, do not destroy it: set it aside in the Re-Dreaming pile. At the start of every round, AFTER the Toll advances and zones flip, count the Grief pool.…

lore.origin: The Sediment was not founded; it accreted. Where the other three orders crystallized around scholars, zealots, and merchants — people with names and signatures — the Sediment began the first time a wading archivist died on the flat and the tide, receding past her body, declined to erase her. She rose. Salt-skinned, translucent, remembering nothing but the single moment that held her solid, she walked toward the nearest pool as if drawn to a hearth. The hierophants of the…
lore.culture: They have no archives, because to archive is to fix, and to fix is to refuse the god its rest. Instead they keep middens — sprawling, deliberately disorganized heaps of un-set salt-glass left loose in the wet so the tide can take any of it at any time. A Sediment camp is identifiable by the absence of locks, walls, and ledgers, and by the constant low chorus of the salt-dead murmuring the one moment each can still remember, over and over, until the sound becomes a kind of…
lore.whyTheyFight: They do not fight to win the past. They fight to ensure no one else fixes it, because every Set crystal is a thought the god is forbidden to release — a splinter driven into a dying mind to keep it awake and in pain. The Mnemarchs call this preservation; the Sediment calls it the cruelest thing in the world. Their war aim is not victory but completion: they want the Long Toll to strike Dry with as much history as possible still loose, dissolving, free to return to solution…
lore.leadership: There is no hierarch, because hierarchy is a structure and structures are fixed. The Sediment is led, loosely and reluctantly, by the Grief-Touched: living hierophants so deep into iodine-blindness that they have begun to weep brine and shed salt at the fingertips, halfway to becoming Reliquiae themselves. The eldest of these is called the Undertow — a title, not a name, because whoever holds it has forgotten their name on purpose. The Undertow does not give orders so much…
lore.homeland: The Lees — the lowest, oldest, most thoroughly evaporated quarter of the Litany Sea, where the brine receded first and the salt lies deepest. It is a sunken plain of fossil tide-lines, ankle-deep where it is wet at all, studded with the standing salt-figures of Reliquiae who walked there in ages past and simply stopped, too far from any pool to stay solid, frozen mid-stride forever. The living call it the boneyard; the Sediment calls it the Nursery, because the Lees is where…

units.name: Wadeling Drift
units.flavor: The freshly-risen, wading in loose drifts to smother crystals in translucent numbers — the cheapest re-dreaming in the order.

units.name: Tide-Drowned Bulwark
units.flavor: Ancient Lees-dead grown into walking statues, planting themselves in the wet to cushion a Drowned prize and dare the Dry to take them.

units.name: Lees-Walker Vigilants
units.flavor: Nursery zealots who march into the lethal Dry to stand vigil on enemy Set crystals, cracking permanence open by their desecrating presence.

units.name: Brine-Wet Cantor
units.flavor: An apostate ex-Factor or broken ex-Mnemarch who reads the Long Toll like a market, naming which zone drowns or dries ahead of its band.

units.name: Murmur-Host
units.flavor: A tide of Reliquiae packed shoulder to translucent shoulder, smothering whole zones in slowed, grieving bodies where no one runs.

units.name: Standing Salt (Erasure-Born)
units.flavor: The largest re-dreamings — moments so vast the god's flinch returns them outsized and terrible, surging up only when the Grief pool runs deep.

units.name: The Stranded
units.flavor: Reliquiae fed into the deep Dry on purpose, racing the second tide to spend one last moment striking where no dead should reach.

units.name: Salt-Stranded Drowner
units.flavor: Mid-deep Reliquiae whose one remembered moment is of carrying something heavy into water — they exist to drag the prize into the shrinking brine.

units.name: Iodine-Blind Chorister
units.flavor: A living-dead tender of the middens who shatters its own loose salt-glass to feed the Grief pool faster — history spent as kindling for the horde.

characters.name: The Undertow
characters.title: Eldest Grief-Touched Hierophant
characters.flavor: The order's reluctant head, weeping brine from blind eyes and dissolving into a Reliquia in real time — and welcoming it. Its fall re-dreams a tide.

characters.name: Maren Eb, the Twice-Wet
characters.title: Brine-Wet Cantor-Prime (apostate Brine-Factor)
characters.flavor: An ex-Factor edited past the thread of her own sales, now reading the Long Toll like a ledger and stranding the living in the catastrophes she calls early.

scenarios.name: The Reckoning of the Sixth Toll
scenarios.hook: Veyl is dying with the tide. For six hundred years the Litany Sea has covered the Choir-Floor of Saint Marrow's Reach, and for six hundred years the crystals set into that floor have stayed solid, wet, and unreadable — a library nobody could open because…
scenarios.setup: Play on a board divided into SIX numbered tidal bands running parallel to the shore edge, Band 1 (nearest shore) to Band 6 (deepest sea). Each band is covered by a double-sided terrain overlay: WET side up = Brine-deep, DRY side up = exposed Choir-Floor. At game start, ALL six bands are WET (Brine-deep). Place the Tide Track beside the board, a fixed strip of six notches labelled Toll I through Toll VI, with the Tide marker resting before Toll I. Place ONE Litany crystal model in the centre of each band — six crystals total, all starting Loose and all starting in Brine-deep zones (so all six begin shatter-immune). Crystals 1-2 are minor (1 Shatter destroys), crystals 3-4 are major (2…
scenarios.deployment: Four-player free-for-all. The three living factions (Mnemarchs, Ash Iconoclasts, Brine-Factors) deploy along the SHORE edge only, within 6" of the board edge behind Band 1 — i.e. on dry land, with the entire wet sea between them and the deepest crystals. Roll off for deployment order; place alternately. No living model may begin in a Brine-deep band (you start on the shore and must advance into the receding tide as it opens). The Sediment (Veyl's swarm) does not deploy a starting force; the Sediment player instead takes the Grief pool and the Salt-dead reserve, and re-dreams Reliquiae onto the board as the Long Toll opens Dry ground for them (see Special Rules). The shore edge belongs to no…
scenarios.objectives: Primary: control the most VALUE in INTACT crystals when the Sixth Toll strikes Dry and the game ends. A crystal scores for the player whose model is in base contact (Held), who has Set it (Mnemarch), or who has Liquidated it to the Hold (Brine-Factor) — a Loose crystal nobody controls scores for nobody, and a Shattered crystal scores for nobody and never did. Each living faction races the silent Toll Deck to LOCK value in before a rival contests it: Mnemarchs Set crystals in WET bands (sealed forever); Brine-Factors carry Loose crystals to the shore and Liquidate them into Coin (off-board, unsealable, un-re-dreamable); Iconoclasts deny all value by Shattering Exposed crystals in DRY bands…
scenarios.twist: The tide does not drain in band order — it drains in a SECRET PROGRAMMED SEQUENCE revealed one notch at a time. Before the game, shuffle six band-tiles (numbered 1-6) face down into a Toll Deck. At the START of each round, before any activation, flip the top Toll Deck tile: THAT band flips from Wet…

scenarios.name: The Reliquary Run
scenarios.hook: When the Sea first began to leave, the Mnemarchs hid their holiest Litany — the Choir-Crystal called Nine Mouths, which remembers the exact sound Veyl made when it learned its dead were dead — in the deepest brine-pit on the shelf, trusting the water to guard…
scenarios.setup: Play on a roughly 4x4 board divided into a 4x4 grid of sixteen zones. Build the board entirely from double-sided terrain overlays (wet side up / dry side up) so every zone can flip on the Toll. At game start, the OUTER ring of twelve zones is Brine-deep (wet side up); the inner 2x2 of four zones — the Choir-Pit — is also Brine-deep. Place crystal models as physical objects: ONE Choir-Crystal (Nine Mouths, a large model, the Prize) Loose at the dead center of the Choir-Pit, and FIVE lesser Litany crystals Loose, one in each of five randomly chosen outer zones. All six crystals begin in Brine-deep zones, so all six begin protected (AUTO-PASS shatter). Set up the Tide Track at 6 tides. Place…
scenarios.deployment: Four factions, four board edges, deployed in that turn order: Mnemarchs, Brine-Factors, Ash Iconoclasts, Sediment. The first three deploy along their own board edge, no model within one zone of any crystal. The Sediment do NOT deploy a force — instead the Sediment player places NOTHING at start and is given the Grief pool: they bring models onto the board only by Re-dreaming Reliquiae out of drying pits (see special rules). The Choir-Crystal at center is equidistant from all three edge factions by design — nobody can reach it before the tide does.
scenarios.objectives: The prize is custody of intact history, not a body count. Crystals score ONLY for the faction that controls them in their winning custody state when the Toll strikes Dry. A shattered crystal scores for NO ONE — it never happened. Each faction scores its OWN custody state: Mnemarchs score Set crystals; Brine-Factors score crystals taken OFF the board into the Hold; Iconoclasts score crystals they personally Shattered; Sediment score crystals that are Loose in a Dry zone they occupy (Drowned). The Choir-Crystal (Nine Mouths) is worth triple any lesser Litany to whoever's victory state it ends in.
scenarios.twist: THE PIT REMEMBERS WHAT IT DROWNED. The Choir-Crystal, Nine Mouths, sits in the last pit to dry — and it is not empty. When tide 6 flips the Choir-Pit to Dry and the Prize finally surfaces Exposed, the Grief pool DISCHARGES: the Sediment player immediately Re-dreams up to their full Grief total of…

scenarios.name: The Sealing of the Last Shoal
scenarios.hook: Veyl's grief dreams loudest at the Last Shoal, a reef of seven Litany-crystals that holds the only un-erased memory of the god's first death. The Sealing Choir of the Mnemarchs has waded out at low brine to perform the Set Hour and lock the Shoal beyond all…
scenarios.setup: Play on a 4x4 board divided into six numbered tide bands (1 nearest the dry shore, 6 furthest out to sea). Every band starts Brine-deep (wet side up) EXCEPT band 1, which begins Dry. Place SEVEN Litany-crystal models in a rough arc across the Shoal: one each in bands 1 and 6, two in band 2, and three clustered in bands 3 and 4 (the heart of the reef). All seven crystals begin Loose and Un-set. Build a physical Tide Track of six notches; place the Tide marker on notch 1. Place an empty Grief pool dish beside the board. Each band is a double-sided terrain overlay: wet side up = Brine-deep (auto-pass shatter, no Set possible), dry side up = Dry (Exposed crystals, Sealing possible). Set aside a…
scenarios.deployment: ASYMMETRIC. The MNEMARCHS (defender) deploy first, anywhere in bands 4, 5, and 6 (the still-wet heart and seaward edge of the Shoal), in base contact with or within 3 inches of the crystals they intend to seal. The defender may declare any number of models as Choristers at deployment. The ASH ICONOCLASTS (attacker) deploy second, entirely along the dry shore edge behind band 1 — they begin on land, the wrong side of the water, and must advance INTO the receding sea as it dries before them. No attacker model may deploy past the band-1/band-2 line. The attacker has the first activation of round 1.
scenarios.objectives: The crystals are the only objective; ground is worthless. A crystal scores for the side that owns its final state when the Toll strikes Dry. A crystal is SEALED (scores for the Mnemarchs) if a Chorister completed the Set Hour on it. A crystal is SILENCED (scores for the Iconoclasts) if it was Shattered and removed. A crystal that ends the game Loose, Un-set, and intact scores for NEITHER side. Count Sealed crystals for the defender and Silenced crystals for the attacker at the final Toll.
scenarios.twist: THE SHOAL DROWNS ITSELF. The Iconoclasts cannot simply rush band 1, because Shattering feeds the Grief pool — and the Grief horde belongs to the attacker to place but answers to no one's victory. Every crystal Shattered and every band that flips Dry drops a token in the Grief pool. At the start of…

scenarios.name: The Last Liquidation
scenarios.hook: When the Long Toll reads four-of-six, the Brine-Factors call a Liquidation: one crystal, the Vault-Heart, holds a moment so old that no Choir has dared seal it and no Scour has dared shatter it — and now the tide that protected it is leaving. The Factors mean…
scenarios.setup: Play on a 3 x 3 ft table. Lay 6-10 terrain pieces, then overlay a fixed Tide Track of 6 notches along one table edge where every player can see it. Divide the board into six numbered Tide Bands running parallel to the tideline (Band 1 nearest the dry shore, Band 6 nearest the deep). At the start, Bands 1-2 are Dry (dry side of the terrain overlay up) and Bands 3-6 are Brine-deep (wet side up). Place ONE special crystal model, the Vault-Heart, dead centre in Band 4 (Brine-deep, so it starts auto-protected and Loose). Place two ordinary Loose crystals, one each in Band 3 and Band 5. Set out a single shared Grief pool dish beside the Tide Track with a reserve of tokens. Each player nominates…
scenarios.deployment: Roll off. The winner picks a long table edge as their Extraction Edge; the loser takes the opposite. (In a 3-4 player game, each player takes a quarter and a corner Extraction Edge.) Players then alternate placing one model at a time within 6 inches of their own edge. NO model may be deployed in Band 4 or in any Brine-deep band adjacent to the Vault-Heart — everyone starts on the dry margins and must wade inward as the tide that guards the prize drains away. Scouts/infiltrators deploy last but may not be placed in a Brine-deep band. The Vault-Heart and the two ordinary crystals are placed during Setup, before any models.
scenarios.objectives: This is an extraction-and-denial mission, not a body count. Your goal is to fix the Custody fate of the Vault-Heart at the moment the Toll strikes Dry. Three mutually exclusive winning fates exist: EXTRACTED (a Held carrier walks it off your own Extraction Edge — it becomes Coin), DROWNED (a Held carrier spends its whole activation to shove the crystal one band deeper into a still-Brine-deep band and let go — it sinks beyond all custody), or SEALED (a ritual completes it in place in a wet band — Set forever). If the Vault-Heart is still Loose on the table when the Toll strikes Dry in its band it is Exposed to the swarm. Carrying it is an IGNORE tradeoff: a model in base contact may pick it…
scenarios.twist: THE WATER LEAVES THE TABLE. At the start of every round the Tide marker advances one mandatory, unskippable notch and ALL of one numbered Band flips from Brine-deep to Dry via the double-sided overlay: Round 2 flips Band 3, Round 3 flips Band 4 (the Vault-Heart's home — the hinge of the game),…

scenarios.name: The Undertow Verdict
scenarios.hook: This is the deepest receding the Litany Sea has ever dared: a spring ebb that bares the drowned cathedral floor in three falling stages, and with it the worst of Veyl's dreaming grief. The Ash Iconoclasts came to silence the cathedral for good. The Sediment…
scenarios.setup: Play on a 4x4 board divided into a 6x6 zone grid: the drowned cathedral floor. Lay the double-sided wet/dry overlays so the central 3x4 block of zones (the nave) begins Brine-deep, and the surrounding aisle ring begins Dry. Place 8 crystals, the Litany of the cathedral: 5 in the wet nave, 3 scattered loose across the dry aisles. Set a Tide Track of 6 notches, and mark notches 2 and 4 with a colored band: these are the two STAGE BREAKS. Pre-define the dry-flip bands so the nave recedes from the OUTSIDE IN: the aisle-facing nave zones flip first (notches 1 and 2), the deep center flips last (notches 5 and 6), the inverse of an ordinary ebb. The Grief pool starts at zero. Place a Hold box off…
scenarios.deployment: Diagonal deployment. The Ash Iconoclasts and the Sediment deploy in OPPOSITE corners, each confined to a 10-inch quadrant: they are the axis of this fight and must stare across the whole board at each other. The Mnemarchs and the Brine-Factors deploy along the two remaining board edges, within 6 inches of their edge. No model may begin in a Brine-deep zone (you cannot start standing in the Sea). After deployment, whichever faction has the FEWEST models on the board takes the first activation: the underdog reads the water first.
scenarios.objectives: Scoring changes by stage, and the Toll decides the stage. A crystal can only ever be claimed ONCE, by the first method that fully resolves on it. STAGE ONE (rounds 1-2, the Choir's Hour): only SET crystals (Mnemarchs) and LIQUIDATED crystals taken into Hold (Brine-Factors) score. These are wet-side acts. STAGE TWO (rounds 3-4, the Breaking Hour): only SHATTERED crystals (Ash Iconoclasts) and DROWNED crystals re-covered into play (Sediment) score. These are dry-side acts; Setting and Liquidating still physically happen but bank zero points this stage. STAGE THREE (rounds 5-6, the Undertow): ALL four methods score again, and every crystal whose fate is recorded on the Undertow Track scores…
scenarios.twist: At the second Stage Break (the start of round 5, the Undertow proper), the deepest nave zones, the last wet ground and the safest crystals all game, begin to dry from the CENTER OUTWARD, reversing every prior tide. The crystals everyone treated as untouchable vault stock are Exposed all at once,…
